| Elbow Joint | 
1. Elbow Flexion |  | 
Subject Test Position • Subject in sitting, with back supported • Shoulder neutral • Forearm supinated Goniometer Alignment • Axis – lateral epicondyle of humerus • Stationary arm – aligned humerus (center of acromion process) • Moving arm – aligned with radius (styloid process) Action Ask the subject to bend the elbow |  | 
2. Elbow Extension |  | 
Subject Test Position • Subject in sitting, with back supported • Shoulder neutral • Forearm supinated Goniometer Alignment • Axis – lateral epicondyle of humerus • Stationary arm – aligned humerus (center of acromion process) • Moving arm – aligned with radius (styloid process) Action Ask the subject to straighten the elbow |  | 
 | Wrist Joint | 
1. Wrist Flexion |  | 
Subject Test Position • Subject sitting • Forearm stabilized on table with palm facing down Goniometer Alignment • Axis – lateral wrist • Stationary arm – aligned with ulna • Moving arm – aligned with fifth metacarpal Action • Ask the subject to flex the wrist (fingers relaxed) |  | 
2. Wrist Extension |  |

1. Pronation |  | 
Subject Test Position • Subject sitting • Shoulder neutral • Elbow fixed at 90° • Palm in neutral position Goniometer Alignment • Axis – lateral to ulnar styloid process • Stationary arm – parallel to humerus • Moving arm – aligned with dorsal aspect of wrist Action Ask the subject to pronate the forearm |  |

Subject Test Position • Subject sitting • Shoulder neutral • Elbow fixed at 90° • Hold a pen in the fist at neutral position Goniometer Alignment • Axis – medial to ulnar styloid • Stationary arm – parallel to humerus • Moving arm – aligned with the pen Action Ask the subject to supinate the forearm |  |

4. Ulnar Deviation |  | 
Subject Test Position • Subject sitting with forearm resting on table, palm facing down Goniometer Alignment • Axis – capitate (middle of wrist joint) • Stationary arm – aligned with forearm (lateral epicondyle) • Moving arm – aligned with metacarpal of middle finger Action Ask the subject to do ulnar deviation |  | 
 | Fingers | 
1. Metacarpophalangeal Joint Flexion (MCP flexion) |  | 
Subject Test Position • Subject sitting with forearm resting on table • Wrist and interphalangeal joints relaxed • Forearm neutral Goniometer Alignment • Place the finger goniometer over the Dorsal MCP joint • Stationary arm - aligned with metacarpal • Moving arm – aligned with proximal phalange Action Ask the subject to flex the MCP joint |  | 
 | Hip Joint | 
1. Hip Flexion |  | 
Subject Test Position • Subject Supine • Allow knee to flex (to avoid limitation by tight hamstrings) Goniometer Alignment • Axis – greater trochanter • Stationary arm – aligned with midline of pelvis • Moving arm – aligned with femur (lateral epicondyle) Action |  |
